prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a paved road and striped parking area in the immediate foreground (roughly 1 to 5 metres away, brightest at the bottom) bordered by raised curbs on the left and right, with a small log cabin and coniferous trees at intermediate distances (about 6 to 15 metres) and a deeper wooded park receding beyond 20 metres. In frames 2 and 3, as the camera wearer turns first rightward and then back toward the left across the sequence, a person on a skateboard appears on the right at roughly 5 to 7 metres from the camera wearer, positioned about 3 to 5 metres in front of a parked silver car that sits further right and behind them at around 9 to 12 metres. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer rotates their view to the right in frames 2–3 and then pans back left while moving forward along the curving road in frames 4–5, causing the log cabin and pine tree to shift from the right side of frame 1 to the left side of frame 3 and back to the right in frames 4–5; nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouette of the skateboarder and individual tree trunks from the shadowed background foliage and dark cabin walls, though it fails to capture painted road markings or the person's facial orientation toward the camera wearer. The depth map is unreliable around thin tree branches and canopy gaps where sky bleeds into foliage, and it flattens the distant parked car in frames 2–3 into the surrounding ground plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground objects in frames 2, 3, and 5 while leaving the road, curbs, and trees unlabelled, identifying the person on the right in frames 2 and 3 (roughly 5 to 7 metres away, facing and looking generally toward the camera wearer) and the parked car partially occluded behind them to the right at about 9 to 12 metres. In frame 2, a small object within arm's reach of the person's right hand is labelled as a handbag, and in frame 3 the board beneath their feet is labelled as a skateboard while a second tiny car mask appears at the far right edge, with the car partially cut off by the frame boundary. As the camera wearer pans right into frames 2–3 and then turns back left in frames 4–5, the person and car shift to the right edge of the view in frame 3 and exit the field of view completely in frames 4 and 5, while nothing enters within arm's reach of the camera wearer. This map highlights the small handheld item in frame 2, the skateboard under the person's feet in frame 3, and the occluded car behind the person in dark tree shadows that are hard to distinguish at a glance in the RGB strip. However, it is highly unreliable across the sequence: it misses the skateboard in frame 2, misclassifies the dark log cabin on the right side of frame 5 (about 8 to 10 metres away) as a bench, and fails to segment the cabin in frames 1, 3, and 4 or any background buildings.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, detecting neither body skeletons nor hand keypoints anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, a person is visible on the right side of frames 2 and 3 at roughly 5 to 7 metres from the camera wearer (standing about 3 to 5 metres in front of a parked car), oriented with their torso and head facing toward the camera wearer and their hands hanging near their hips within arm's reach of a small carried item, before passing out of view to the right as the camera wearer turns left in frames 4 and 5. The camera wearer's own body and hands remain entirely outside the camera's field of view throughout the sequence, with no objects within the camera wearer's arm's reach. Consequently, the pose map adds no spatial information beyond the RGB frames and is completely unreliable for the person in frames 2 and 3, failing to detect their upright posture, limb positions, or gaze direction due to their ~5 to 7 metre distance and the harsh dappled shadows cast by the surrounding trees.
